ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is the volume of added HCl, and the vertical axis is pH. As the volume of HCl increases, pH gradually decreases from a higher value, and an obvious steep vertical drop appears near about 22–24 mL; the midpoint of the steep-drop section represents the pH near the titration endpoint, and this pH is lower than 7. Reasoning: A visual indicator should undergo a color change near the endpoint pH; since indicators usually change color when pH is close to their pKa, an indicator with pKa close to the endpoint pH should be selected.

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: pH decreases as HCl volume increases, with a sharp vertical drop near the endpoint. Identify the pH at the middle of that steep drop as the endpoint pH. Then choose the indicator property that makes its color change occur at that same pH: its pKa should be close to the endpoint pH.
